newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich hearings delayed after Democrats complain.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich hearings delayed after Democrats complain.

text.p: Republicans on the House Ethics Committee, bowing to Democrats' protests on Thursday night, abruptly changed plans for hearings on ethics charges against House Speaker Newt Gingrich.

Democrats had complained that the House was being asked to vote on Jan. 21 on a punishment for Gingrich's admitted ethics violations before the committee's special counsel James Cole had completed his report on the case.

Hours after committee Democrats held a news conference to protest the schedule, the panel's Republican chairwoman, Representative Nancy Johnson of Connecticut, told reporters they had instructed Cole to advance the release of his report to Jan. 16.
Johnson said in a statement that public hearings would be held after the release of the report instead of Monday to Friday next week. The specific dates and times for the hearings were not announced.
Gingrich was narrowly re-elected House Speaker on Tuesday, with 11 Republicans refusing to vote for him because of his admitted ethics violations.
After the committee originally scheduled five days of televised hearings next week, Democrats on the panel complained they were being asked to vote on a punishment before getting all the facts.

Democratic Whip David Bonior also suggested Republicans were seeking to time key actions in the last phase of the two-year investigation so they would be overshadowed by other events, such as President Clinton's Jan. 20 inauguration.
"Republicans are trying to slide this case under the rug," he said.

Democrat George Miller of California had proposed House resolutions to delay the punishment until after the report was publicly released and to require that all documents in the case be released. "This schedule is ludicrous," he said.
The committee's original plan was issued early on Thursday morning following a meeting lasting more than 13 hours.
Johnson said on Thursday night that the committee had worked those hours "in good faith" to produce a schedule to complete work on the Gingrich case.
"Today at their press conference, Democrats said this schedule was wrong -- that the final report of the committee was more important than public hearings," she said in announcing the change.
Speculation is that the committee will call for a reprimand -- a lesser punishment than expulsion or censure and one that would not require the speaker to step down.
The House in the past has strengthened recommended reprimands to censures.

Gingrich admitted on Dec. 21 he had failed to get legal advice to ensure compliance with a ban on using tax-exempt funds for partisan political activity and had given false information to investigators.
